designationHistory.indexText: Established in 1968 after The Nature Conservancy bought St. Vincent Island and the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service repaid it with Duck Stamp funds.

authority.citation: Migratory Bird Conservation Act (Duck Stamp funds)

designationHistory.note: The refuge page gives only the month or year.

sources.name: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service: St. Vincent National Wildlife Refuge, About Us

FWS St. Vincent NWR general brochure (archived 2013): island bought by The Nature Conservancy for $2.2 million, repaid with Duck Stamp funds; "Established as St. Vincent National Wildlife Refuge" in 1968

review.note: Draft took a timeline line about the Port of Apalachicola (1822) and "Native Americans" as signer. Refuge dates to 1968. Source is an older FWS brochure; confirm with the CCP if possible.

designationHistory.indexOriginal: Up until the Port of Apalachicola was established in 1822, land around the Apalachicola area was occupied by Native Americans.

historySource: Refuge About Us pages, fws.gov (draft, pending review)
